lessons.title: Active vs Passive Voice
lessons.concept: In active voice, the subject performs the action (e.g., 'The teacher explains the lesson'). In passive voice, the subject receives the action (e.g., 'The lesson is explained by the teacher'). The object of the active sentence often becomes the subject in the passive sentence.
lessons.formula: Active: Subject + verb + object. Passive: Object (as subject) + form of 'be' + past participle (+ by + agent).
lessons.worked_example: Active: 'Rita wrote a letter.' Passive: 'A letter was written by Rita.'
mistakes: Keeping the same subject position without changing verb form
Forgetting to use past participle in passive voice
Dropping or misusing 'by' when the agent is needed
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Tense Changes in Passive Voice
lessons.concept: When converting active to passive, the tense is preserved using an appropriate form of 'be' plus the past participle. The main verb changes form, but the time meaning remains the same.
lessons.formula: Simple present: is/am/are + V3. Simple past: was/were + V3. Present continuous: is/am/are + being + V3. Present perfect: has/have + been + V3.
lessons.worked_example: Active (simple present): 'She cleans the room.' Passive: 'The room is cleaned by she' (incorrect pronoun form in by-phrase) -> 'The room is cleaned by her.' Active (simple past): 'He repaired the car.' Passive: 'The car was repaired by him.'
mistakes: Using wrong 'be' form (is/are/was/were) for subject and tense
Using base verb instead of past participle (V3)
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Using Passive Voice Appropriately
lessons.concept: Passive voice is useful when the doer is unknown, unimportant, or obvious, or when focus is on the action/receiver. Not all sentences should be converted; choose voice based on clarity and emphasis.
lessons.formula: Use passive when focus is on receiver/action: 'The window was broken.' (doer unknown) Active when doer is important: 'The child broke the window.'
lessons.worked_example: Unknown doer: 'My phone was stolen yesterday.' Focus on process/result: 'The results will be announced tomorrow.'
mistakes: Assuming passive voice is always better/formal
Creating unclear sentences by omitting necessary agent information
Forcing passive conversion where object is absent (intransitive verbs)
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: Change to passive voice: 'The chef cooks the meal.'

options.A: The meal is cooked by the chef.
options.B: The meal was cooked by the chef.
options.C: The meal cooks by the chef.
options.D: The chef is cooked the meal.

practice.explanation: Simple present active becomes is/am/are + past participle in passive: 'cooks' -> 'is cooked'. Object 'the meal' becomes subject.

practice.explanation: Simple past active ('wrote') becomes was/were + past participle ('was written') in passive voice.

practice.question: Change to passive voice: 'They are painting the house.'

options.B: The house was being painted by them.

options.D: The house has been painted by them.

practice.explanation: Present continuous active becomes is/am/are + being + past participle in passive: 'are painting' -> 'is being painted'.
